title: Boiler-2 Commanded On But Fails to Prove
description: Boiler Manager stages Boiler-2 on for additional heating demand, but Boiler-2 never proves -- simulating a failed ignition attempt.

events.description: Represent a failed start/ignition-permissive circuit: BACnet accepts the start command but the burner sequence never receives it
Boiler Manager stages Boiler-2 on for additional demand
Start Boiler-2's required circulator so ignition has valid flow
Start the building hot-water distribution pump

expected_results: Boiler Manager's Enable Boiler2 command and Boiler-2's own Boiler S/S command both show on
Boiler-2 OK never transitions to proven, firing rate remains zero, and Boiler-2 adds no heat even well past the normal purge+ignition delay
WebCTRL should eventually alarm on failed-to-prove, matching how a real ignition lockout would present
Boiler-1 and Boiler-3 are unaffected -- this is isolated to one unit
completion_criteria: Student recognizes the failure pattern (commanded on, never proves) rather than assuming a comms failure
Student checks the other two boilers to confirm this is unit-specific, not a Boiler Manager problem
instructor_notes: The failure is applied to the simulated start/ignition input rather than merely forcing a proof sensor off. That prevents false-status training in which a hidden boiler would still fire and heat the loop. Pump flow and pump heat remain physically present. Use STOP/RESET after diagnosis.
student_objectives: Diagnose a failed-to-prove condition on a specific piece of staged equipment
Correctly scope the problem to one unit rather than the whole boiler plant
